text: PwnKit Privilege Escalation (CVE-2021-4034)

PwnKit is a local privilege escalation vulnerability in <highlight>polkit's pkexec</highlight>. If the binary is vulnerable, a low‑privileged user can exploit it to execute commands as <highlight>root</highlight>.
Initial Foothold
The system was compromised and a low‑privilege shell was obtained as the <highlight>www-data</highlight> user.
Checking pkexec Version
The system is running a version of pkexec that may be vulnerable to <highlight>PwnKit</highlight>.
Checking if pkexec is SUID
The <highlight>s</highlight> flag confirms that the binary is running with <highlight>SUID root privileges</highlight>, meaning it executes as root even when run by normal users.
Uploading PwnKit Exploit
The PwnKit exploit was uploaded to the writable directory <highlight>/dev/shm</highlight>.
Running the Exploit

code: Failed to copy file: File exists

text: The exploit attempted to trigger the vulnerability by abusing the GCONV_PATH environment variable used by pkexec.
Discovering Backup Files
A backup of the user <highlight>mike</highlight>'s home directory was discovered inside the system backups.
Reading User Bash History

code:
cd ~
ls
ping 1.1.1.1
cat /home/mike/user.txt
cd /var/www/
ls
cd html
ls -al
cat index.html
sudo -lb3stpassw0rdbr0xx
clear
sudo -l
exit

text: The bash history revealed that the user <highlight>mike</highlight> executed sudo commands and exposed a password in the command line.
Finding a Root-Owned Script
The script allows reading the file <highlight>/root/report.txt</highlight> using the nano editor.
Opening Root File With Nano
Because the script runs with elevated privileges, opening the file through nano allows interacting with a root-owned file.
Escaping Nano to Get a Shell
Nano allows command execution features that can be abused to spawn a shell when opened with elevated privileges.
Root Access Obtained
